source_review.notes: Checked current Trino dynamic-filtering, optimizer, and pushdown documentation; current Spark SQL performance/configuration, Iceberg partitioning, Parquet page-index, ORC specification, and Velox operator documentation; the primary Bloom-filter paper; and primary F1 Query, Presto, and Dremel accounts. All thirteen final references returned HTTP 200. An ACM DOI returning HTTP 403 was excluded in favor of an accessible archival copy of the primary Bloom paper. Product behavior is attributed, and performance recommendations are conditional on measured timing, selectivity, granularity, and cost.

evidence: Reviewed probe/build key functions, completed build-key set, filter implication, bit count, distinct-key count, hash count, and false-positive probability.
Reviewed exact-set union, compatible Bloom bitmap OR, enclosing range merge, logical-task coverage, epochs, and selected attempts.
Checked set membership, implication direction, nonnegative sizes, probability bounds, byte conversion, and scope/completeness qualifiers.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Possible false positives, forbidden false negatives, exact positives, and completed-scope negatives remain distinct.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced bits=100000, memory_bytes=12500, hashes=7, and estimated_fpr=0.0082 for 10,000 keys at 10 bits per key.
Recomputed Exercise 1 as 24,000,000 bits, 3,000,000 bytes, near-optimal k=12 ln 2 approximately 8.32, and idealized p approximately 0.00314 for k=8.
Checked integer rounding is presented as an implementation choice around the continuous optimum rather than a universal guarantee.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Bloom probabilities assume complete insertion, compatible uniform hashes, declared parameters, and no corruption; they do not establish query-level speedup.

evidence: Verified F(x)=false implies x is absent from the complete build-key set is the required one-sided pruning condition.
Derived Bloom p=(1-exp(-kn/m))^k and the continuous optimum k=(m/n) ln 2 under the stated idealized model.
Verified exact summaries merge by set union, compatible Bloom summaries by bitmap OR, and range summaries by global minimum/maximum without narrowing the represented domain.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The implication alone is insufficient without matching join, null, residual, type, snapshot, attempt, and connector semantics.

evidence: Reviewed empty and incomplete builds, duplicates, null and composite keys, coercions, NaN, signed zero, time zones, collations, and residual predicates.
Reviewed inner, outer, semi, ordinary anti, and null-aware anti joins; exact, saturated Bloom, and gapped range filters; and evolving partition transforms.
Reviewed retries, speculation, missing contributions, stale epochs, late arrival, coordinator restart, corruption, connector rejection, cancellation, metadata uncertainty, and resource exhaustion.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Unknown, incompatible, partial, stale, corrupt, or unsupported evidence retains work or disables filtering.

evidence: Traced query, join, build side, snapshot, logical partitions, selected attempts, epoch, type/encoding, algorithm, parameters, and completeness through aggregation and consumption.
Checked only one fenced successful attempt contributes per logical build task and completeness counts logical coverage rather than message count.
Checked pruning at partition, file, row-group/page, split, exchange, batch, and row levels preserves the same conservative semantic contract.
invariant_checking.notes: Timeout, overflow, incompatibility, uncertainty, and recovery fall back to the exact unfiltered execution path.

evidence: Reviewed the safety argument from completed build evidence through one-sided filter implication to target-specific pruning.
Checked why a monotone partial filter is unsafe for negative pruning until its declared scope is complete.
Checked applicability arguments for preserved outer sides, anti joins, null-aware semantics, residuals, adaptive replacement, and connector translation.
proof_review.notes: Soundness, completeness publication, applicability, metadata trust, and economic benefit are treated as separate obligations.

evidence: Audited runtime filter, dynamic filter, dynamic partition pruning, exact set, Bloom filter, range filter, completeness, and pruning-granularity terminology.
Confirmed a Bloom positive is not labeled proof of membership and a range hit is not labeled exact membership.
Confirmed partition, manifest, file, stripe, row group, page, split, exchange partition, batch, and row pruning are not conflated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Filter type, evidence scope, target granularity, join applicability, and publication state are explicitly named.

evidence: Reviewed filter build/merge/distribution/wait cost, memory, selectivity, false positives, late-filter timing, target work avoided, critical path, and monetary cost.
Confirmed no universal bits-per-key, wait duration, size cap, fan-in, broadcast threshold, selectivity cutoff, or pruning target is prescribed.
Confirmed production acceptance requires differential/property tests, fault injection, shadow decisions, canaries, connector cohorts, kill switch, and rollback.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Rows rejected and filter selectivity are not mislabeled as bytes saved, latency reduction, or cluster-level cost improvement.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed filter semantics and lineage, exact/Bloom/range structures, distributed completeness and merge, join applicability, pruning layers, storage formats and evolving partitions, connector contracts, timing, bounded state, retries, security, observability, validation, and rollout.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable epoch/attempt fencing, logical-task coverage, compatible merge rules, conservative connector negotiation, wait-versus-scan policy, bounded coordinator state, overflow fallback, late-filter attribution, tenant isolation, shadow verification, canarying, kill switch, and rollback. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from the no-false-negative contract and filter structures through distributed execution, join semantics, storage/connector boundaries, operations, and validation. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover safety, completeness, Bloom sizing, aggregation, join applicability, evolving partitions, timing, retries, security, metrics, and rollout.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Trino/Spark/Iceberg/Parquet/ORC/Velox maintainer, Bloom/F1/Presto/Dremel author, query-engine or connector operator, probabilistic-data-structure/database/distributed-systems/storage/platform/SRE/performance/security specialist, affected user, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
